audit.whatIsWrong: Rated FAV 7.5/10, and the level chart gave Cho'Gath levels 3, 4-5 and both item stages while handing Wukong level 6. The win rate is 51-52% over 543 games and the page's own whys say the opposite at four of those stages.
audit.why: whys[2] says 'he still owns the all-in' at level 3, whys[3] says the lane 'levels out' at 4-5, whys[4] says Feast deters his all-in at 6, and whys[6] says 'neither outscales the other'. The chart and the prose disagreed stage for stage.
audit.corrected: EVEN, 5.5/10; chart Skill / Wukong / Wukong / Skill / Cho'Gath / Cho'Gath / Skill with ratings 5,4,4,5,6,6,5.

audit.whatIsWrong: Every spike was described without a cooldown, and Warrior Trickster was treated as a clone only.
audit.why: His punish windows are numeric: Warrior Trickster 22/21/20/19/18s, Nimbus Strike 10/9.25/8.5/7.75/7s, Crushing Blow 8 down to 6s, Cyclone 130/110/90s. The 22-second W is the longest and the most exploitable.
audit.corrected: Levels 2-3 are his on Crushing Blow's armour shred; 6 and first item are yours; the fight windows are keyed to Warrior Trickster's 22 seconds.

audit.whatIsWrong: Warrior Trickster's invisibility was never stated - the page only calls it a clone. Crushing Blow was never identified as an auto-attack reset, and Cyclone's 315-unit radius was never given.
audit.why: Riot's text: 'Wukong becomes Invisible and dashes in a direction, leaving behind a clone'. Cho'Gath has no stealth reveal, so the W is a genuine disengage and not just a decoy. Crushing Blow is flagged autoReset, so the wind-up is the burst tell, and it gains attack range up to 350 - further than your auto.
audit.corrected: Feral Scream denies Warrior Trickster and Nimbus Strike; hold Rupture and Feast through the clone; treat the Crushing Blow wind-up as the cue to step back.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Fight his clone' was listed as a mistake but the cost was never quantified.
audit.why: Feast is 175 range on an 80-second cooldown at rank 1, so spending it on a decoy is the single most expensive error available in this matchup.
audit.corrected: Named the range and the cooldown in the don'ts.

edits.before: Wukong owns the early skirmish here — his empowered Q (Crushing Blow) shreds your armor and his E (Nimbus Strike) dashes the gap before your slow Rupture can land, so the level 2-3 window is his to abuse. Do not throw Q on cooldown into auto range or he dashes in during the cast delay and trades you down. Last-hit on Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes, hold Feral Scream's silence for the moment he commits his E, and concede a little health rather than feed a kill.
edits.after: Wukong owns the early skirmish. Crushing Blow is an auto-attack reset that gains range up to 350 - further than your own auto - and shreds your armour for the trade that follows, while Nimbus Strike dashes 650 onto you on a 10-second cooldown. The wind-up on that attack, not the cast bar, is your cue to step back. Don't throw Rupture on cooldown into his range or he simply dashes in during the cast. Last-hit on Carnivore, hold Feral Scream for the moment he commits, and concede health rather than a kill.

edits.before: By levels 4-5 your Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes waveclear stabilize the lane and it goes even. At 6 you flip the script — Feast is a point-blank true-damage execute that ignores his Stone Skin resistances, so if he E-dashes in to all-in you, Rupture knockup into Feral Scream shuts off his re-engage and Feast threatens the kill outright. Watch the W clone: it spawns when he vanishes, so don't dump Rupture or Feast onto the decoy — wait the half-second and punish the real Wukong.
edits.after: By 4-5 your Carnivore sustain and Vorpal Spikes waveclear stabilise the lane and it goes even. At 6 you flip it: Feast is true damage that ignores every stack of Stone Skin armour, so if he dashes in to all-in you, Rupture into Feral Scream denies both Nimbus Strike and Warrior Trickster and the execute threatens the kill outright. Warrior Trickster is the field to watch - it turns him invisible as well as spawning the clone, so wait the beat and spend Rupture and a 80-second Feast on the real Wukong.

notes: Wukong's kit file is champ-data/_kits/monkeyking.json, not wukong.json - there is also a separate jadewukong.json in the same folder, which I did not use. The packet's suspectName 'Feral Scream's' in spikes[3] is a false positive: it is the correct name in possessive form. Also note chogath.json tags Rupture (Q) with grounding, a tooltip-parse misfire on the words 'Ruptures the ground' (the same false positive hits Malphite Q and Olaf Q), so I did not claim Rupture stops Nimbus Strike or the Warrior Trickster dash - only that Feral Scream denies the casts.
